capacity.caveat: Formula/static examples and focused guard proofs, not aggregate allocation telemetry from these API timings.

limitations: Both complete performance fixtures passed independent Git/physical-state oracles. Full functional/broad certification remains required before adoption/publication.
n3 repeats one fixture per variant; first-on remains n1. Fixed order, warm caches and unmeasured host load prevent statistical/causal-confidence claims. Prior windows are not pooled.
All times are raw milliseconds; byte counts are integer bytes. Phases are inclusive and overlap; never add nested phase/FS durations.

Journal write/read bytes are known JS-API payload counters, not physical IO or all copy traffic. Native fs.copyFile has unknown payload; Git extraction bypasses JS IO counters. Journal sync durations sum awaited API calls, not device/CPU time.
RSS includes worker/harness/GC and outside-API lifetime effects, excludes childGit and sub10ms peaks. RSS is not uniformly lower and does not directly measure cumulative requested buffer capacity.
Storage is equivalent-cycle endpoint logical and OS-reported file-data allocation; it excludes peak/full-volume/MFT/ADS/uniqueCoW/deviceIO costs.
Direct spawn counts exclude unobserved descendants; no process identifiers, private host paths or raw logs are included.
The buffer bound and early-growth rejection are the only source changes; journal/durability format and cleanup remain the same. No product source was modified by this benchmark agent.
